title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: Unified Interface Prior Elicitation main entry point eliciting Gamma hyperprior. Automatically selects appropriate algorithm based input specification. Parameters: Returns: canonical dpprior.result/1 DPprior_fit object. scientific audit fields : Examples:
code: DPprior_fit(   J,                      # Sample size (required)   mu_K = NULL,            # Target E[K_J], unless target_pmf is supplied   var_K = NULL,           # Target Var(K_J) (optional)   confidence = c("medium", "low", "high"),   method = c("A2-MN", "A1", "A2-KL"),   target_pmf = NULL,      # Optional custom PMF target for A2-KL   check_diagnostics = TRUE,   warn_dominance = NULL,  # Deprecated warning adapter   M = 80L,                # Quadrature nodes   verbose = FALSE,   warning_policy = NULL,   a1_projection = c("error", "nearest"),   cv_K = NULL,   K_interval = NULL,   target_K = NULL,   ...                     # Must be empty ) # Primary workflow: construct, review, and fit one canonical target target_K <- DPprior_target_K(J = 50, mu_K = 5, confidence = "medium") fit1 <- DPprior_fit(   J = 50, target_K = target_K, method = "A2-MN",   check_diagnostics = FALSE ) print(fit1) #> DPprior Prior Elicitation Result #> =============================================  #>  #> Schema: dpprior.result/1 #> Method: A2-MN (mode: a2_moment) #> Status: converged; usable: yes; verified: yes #>  #> Target (J = 50): #>   E[K_J]   = 5.0000 #>   Var(K_J) = 10.0000 #>  #> Canonical candidate: #>   alpha ~ Gamma(a = 1.4082, b = 1.0770) #>   Achieved E[K_J] = 5.000000; Var(K_J) = 10.000000 #>   Maximum absolute moment residual = 5.68e-11 #>  #> Canonical guidance: scaled component residuals and independent higher-order verification passed  # Scalar convenience route (the canonical target route above is preferred) fit2 <- DPprior_fit(   J = 50, mu_K = 5, var_K = 10, check_diagnostics = FALSE ) cat("Gamma(", round(fit2$parameters$a, 4), ", ",     round(fit2$parameters$b, 4), ")\n", sep = "") #> Gamma(1.4082, 1.077)  # Using A1 closed-form (faster for large J) target_A1 <- DPprior_target_K(J = 200, mu_K = 15, var_K = 30) fit3 <- DPprior_fit(   J = 200, target_K = target_A1, method = "A1",   check_diagnostics = FALSE )  # With diagnostics target_diagnostics <- DPprior_target_K(J = 50, mu_K = 5, var_K = 8) fit4 <- DPprior_fit(   J = 50, target_K = target_diagnostics, check_diagnostics = TRUE )  # Custom PMF target; omitted method dispatches to A2-KL target_pmf <- dpois(1:30, lambda = 5) target_pmf <- target_pmf / sum(target_pmf) target_K_pmf <- DPprior_target_K(J = 30, target_pmf = target_pmf) fit5 <- DPprior_fit(   J = 30, target_K = target_K_pmf, check_diagnostics = FALSE )

title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: Construct Canonical Bounded-Discrete K Target Supply exactly one uncertainty source: var_K, confidence, cv_K, K_interval, target_pmf. returned dpprior.target/1 object retains exact support, original request, normalized used values, implied moments, tolerances, verification, provenance. Pass unchanged target_K DPprior_fit().
code: DPprior_target_K(   J, mu_K = NULL, var_K = NULL, confidence = NULL, cv_K = NULL,   K_interval = NULL, target_pmf = NULL, tolerance = 1e-9,   root_control = NULL ) target_K <- DPprior_target_K(J = 50, mu_K = 5, var_K = 8) target_K$used[c("mu_K", "var_K")] #> $mu_K #> [1] 5 #>  #> $var_K #> [1] 8 fit_K <- DPprior_fit(J = 50, target_K = target_K, method = "A2-MN")

title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: Verified Named Weight Inequality Supported named metrics "wsb_tail", "wsb_mean", "wsb_quantile", certified "wmax_tail_upper". Hard mode lambda. decision-ready result requires mode-specific contract, constraint$satisfied, approved status/usable/verified/message quartet. Infeasible, unknown-feasibility, unapproved approximate outcomes signal typed condition whose result retains canonical evidence.
code: DPprior_dual_hard(   fit,   constraint = list(     metric = "wsb_tail", threshold = 0.5,     relation = "<=", bound = 0.30   ),   constraint_tol = list(abs = 1e-6, rel = 1e-6),   M = 80L, M_verify = NULL,   log_bounds = c(-15, 15), control = list(),   allow_approximate = FALSE, ... ) fit_hard <- DPprior_dual_hard(   fit = fit_K,   constraint = list(     metric = "wsb_tail", threshold = 0.5,     relation = "<=", bound = 0.30   ) ) fit_hard$constraint[c("satisfied", "residual", "tolerance")] #> $satisfied #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $residual #> [1] -6.773471e-13 #>  #> $tolerance #> $tolerance$absolute #> [1] 1e-06 #>  #> $tolerance$relative #> [1] 1e-06 #>  #> $tolerance$effective #> [1] 1.3e-06 fit_hard[c("status", "usable", "verified", "message")] #> $status #> [1] "boundary" #>  #> $usable #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $verified #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $message #> [1] "Hard inequality solution passed verification with the constraint active."

title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: Fixed-Scale Soft Trade-target names weight metric, relation, value. lambda mandatory satisfies 0 < lambda <= 1; trade-weight, constraint probability certificate. tradeoff extension records fixed input-derived scales, component losses, total objective. Soft objects contain constraint_satisfied.
code: DPprior_dual_soft(   fit, target, lambda, max_iter = 100L,   M_fit = 80L, M_verify = NULL,   log_bounds = c(-15, 15), control = list(),   allow_approximate = FALSE, start = NULL, ... ) fit_soft <- DPprior_dual_soft(   fit = fit_K,   target = list(     metric = "wsb_tail", threshold = 0.5,     relation = "target", value = 0.30   ),   lambda = 0.7 ) fit_soft$tradeoff[c("lambda", "K_loss", "weight_loss", "total_loss")] #> $lambda #> [1] 0.7 #>  #> $K_loss #> [1] 0.001506737 #>  #> $weight_loss #> [1] 0.02531088 #>  #> $total_loss #> [1] 0.00864798 fit_soft[c("status", "usable", "verified", "message")] #> $status #> [1] "converged" #>  #> $usable #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $verified #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $message #> [1] "soft trade-off optimizer and independent verification passed"

title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: Pre-compute Log Stirling Numbers Computes logarithm unsigned Stirling numbers first kind |s(J,k)||s(J,k)| JJ 0 J_max kk 0 JJ. Parameters: Returns: lower triangular matrix dimension (Jmax+1)×(Jmax+1)(J_{max}+1) \times (J_{max}+1). Entry [J+1, k+1] contains log⁡|s(J,k)|\log|s(J,k)| (using R’s 1-based indexing). Examples:
code: compute_log_stirling(J_max) # Pre-compute for J up to 100 logS <- compute_log_stirling(100)  # Access |s(10,3)| = 9450 s_10_3 <- exp(logS[11, 4]) cat("|s(10,3)| =", round(s_10_3), "\n") #> |s(10,3)| = 1172700  # Verify row sum identity: sum_k |s(J,k)| = J! J <- 6 row_sum <- sum(exp(logS[J+1, 2:(J+1)])) cat("sum |s(6,k)| =", round(row_sum), ", 6! =", factorial(6), "\n") #> sum |s(6,k)| = 720 , 6! = 720

title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: Antoniak Distribution PMF Computes exact conditional PMF P(KJ=k|α)P(K_J = k | \alpha) using Antoniak distribution formula: P(KJ=k|α)=|s(J,k)|⋅αk(α)J P(K_J = k | \alpha) = \frac{|s(J,k)| \cdot \alpha^k}{(\alpha)_J} Parameters: Returns: Numeric vector length J+1J+1 containing P(KJ=k|α)P(K_J = k | \alpha) k=0,1,…,Jk = 0, 1, \ldots, J. Note: P(KJ=0|α)=0P(K_J = 0 | \alpha) = 0 always. Examples:
code: pmf_K_given_alpha(J, alpha, logS, normalize = TRUE) J <- 50 alpha <- 2.0 logS <- compute_log_stirling(J)  # Compute conditional PMF pmf <- pmf_K_given_alpha(J, alpha, logS)  # Find mode mode_k <- which.max(pmf) - 1 cat("Mode of K|α=2:", mode_k, "\n") #> Mode of K|α=2: 7  # Verify normalization cat("PMF sum:", sum(pmf), "\n") #> PMF sum: 1

title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: Conditional Mean via Digamma Computes 𝔼[KJ|α]=α{ψ(α+J)−ψ(α)}\mathbb{E}[K_J | \alpha] = \alpha \{\psi(\alpha + J) - \psi(\alpha)\} using digamma function. Parameters: Returns: Numeric vector conditional means. Examples:
code: mean_K_given_alpha(J, alpha) J <- 50  # Single alpha mean_K_given_alpha(J, 2.0) #> [1] 7.037626  # Vectorized alpha_seq <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10) means <- mean_K_given_alpha(J, alpha_seq) data.frame(alpha = alpha_seq, E_K = round(means, 2)) #>   alpha   E_K #> 1   0.5  2.94 #> 2   1.0  4.50 #> 3   2.0  7.04 #> 4   5.0 12.46 #> 5  10.0 18.34

previous_headings: 2. Exact Computation Functions > 2.3 Conditional Moment Functions
title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: Conditional Variance via Trigamma Computes Var(KJ|α)=μJ(α)−α2{ψ1(α)−ψ1(α+J)}\text{Var}(K_J | \alpha) = \mu_J(\alpha) - \alpha^2 \{\psi_1(\alpha) - \psi_1(\alpha + J)\}. Key Property: Conditional underdispersion always holds: 0<Var(KJ|α)<𝔼[KJ|α] 0 < \text{Var}(K_J | \alpha) < \mathbb{E}[K_J | \alpha] Examples:
code:
var_K_given_alpha(J, alpha) J <- 50 alpha <- 2.0  mu <- mean_K_given_alpha(J, alpha) sigma2 <- var_K_given_alpha(J, alpha)  cat("E[K|α=2] =", round(mu, 4), "
") #> E[K|α=2] = 7.0376 cat("Var(K|α=2) =", round(sigma2, 4), "
") #> Var(K|α=2) = 4.5356 cat("Underdispersion ratio:", round(sigma2/mu, 4), "< 1 ✓
") #> Underdispersion ratio: 0.6445 < 1 ✓

text: Marginal PMF via Quadrature Mixture Computes marginal PMF mixing conditional PMFs α∼Gamma(,b)\alpha \sim \text{Gamma}(,b): P(KJ=k|,b)=∫0∞P(KJ=k|α)⋅ga,b(α)dα P(K_J = k | , b) = \int_0^\infty P(K_J = k | \alpha) \cdot g_{,b}(\alpha) \, d\alpha Examples:

title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: A1 Closed-Form Approximation Fast closed-form solution using negative binomial approximation marginal distribution KJK_J. Key Formulas: =(μK−1)2σK2−(μK−1),b=(μK−1)⋅cJσK2−(μK−1) = \frac{(\mu_K - 1)^2}{\sigma^2_K - (\mu_K - 1)}, \quad b = \frac{(\mu_K - 1) \cdot c_J}{\sigma^2_K - (\mu_K - 1)} cJc_J scaling constant (default: log⁡J\log J). Feasibility Constraint: Requires σK2>μK−1\sigma^2_K > \mu_K - 1. Examples:
code: DPprior_a1(   J,                      # Sample size   mu_K,                   # Target mean   var_K,                  # Target variance   scaling = "log",        # "log", "harmonic", "digamma"   epsilon = 1e-6          # Feasibility projection buffer ) # Basic A1 fit fit_a1 <- DPprior_a1(J = 50, mu_K = 5, var_K = 8) cat("A1 solution: Gamma(", round(fit_a1$parameters$a, 4), ", ",     round(fit_a1$parameters$b, 4), ")\n", sep = "") #> A1 solution: Gamma(4, 3.912)  # Compare scaling methods for (s in c("log", "harmonic", "digamma")) {   fit <- DPprior_a1(50, 5, 8, scaling = s)   cat(sprintf("  %s: cJ = %.4f\n", s,               fit$computation$scaling$values$cJ)) } #>   log: cJ = 3.9120 #>   harmonic: cJ = 4.4792 #>   digamma: cJ = 4.4633

title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: A2-MN Newton Solver Exact Moment Matching Finds (*,b*)(^*, b^*) induced marginal moments exactly match targets. Algorithm: Initialize A1 closed-form Log-parameterize: η=(log⁡,log⁡b)\eta = (\log , \log b) Newton iteration score-based Jacobian Backtracking line search global convergence Convergence: Typically achieves machine-precision accuracy 3-8 iterations. Examples:
code:
DPprior_a2_newton(   J,                      # Sample size   mu_K,                   # Target mean   var_K,                  # Target variance   a0 = NULL,              # Initial shape (from A1 if NULL)   b0 = NULL,              # Initial rate (from A1 if NULL)   tol_F = 1e-8,           # Residual tolerance   tol_step = 1e-10,       # Step size tolerance   max_iter = 20L,   damping = TRUE,         # Backtracking line search   use_fallback = TRUE,    # Nelder-Mead fallback   M = 80L,   verbose = FALSE ) # Exact moment matching fit <- DPprior_a2_newton(J = 50, mu_K = 5, var_K = 8, verbose = TRUE) #> A2-MN calibrated-moment solver #> Target: E[K]=5, Var(K)=8 #> Residual tolerance: absolute 1e-08 + relative 1e-08 * scale #> Fit M=80; independent verification M=160 #> iter 1: standardized RMS 2.61e+07; step 1; rcond 0.119 #> iter 2: standardized RMS 2.25e+07; step 1; rcond 0.14 #> iter 3: standardized RMS 3.07e+06; step 1; rcond 0.155 #> iter 4: standardized RMS 9.72e+04; step 1; rcond 0.156 #> iter 5: standardized RMS 109; step 1; rcond 0.156 #> Final status: converged; method: scaled_log_newton; verification: independent_verification_passed  # Verify exact matching achieved <- exact_K_moments(   50, fit$parameters$a, fit$parameters$b ) cat("
Target vs Achieved:
") #>  #> Target vs Achieved: cat("  E[K]:   5.000000 vs", sprintf("%.10f", achieved$mean), "
") #>   E[K]:   5.000000 vs 5.0000000000 cat("  Var(K): 8.000000 vs", sprintf("%.10f", achieved$var), "
") #>   Var(K): 8.000000 vs 8.0000000000

title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: A2-KL Distribution Matching via KL Divergence Minimizes Kullback-Leibler divergence target PMF induced marginal PMF KJK_J. Target Specification: Examples:
code: DPprior_a2_kl(   J,                      # Sample size   target,                 # Target PMF or list(mu_K, var_K)   method = c("pmf", "chisq"),  # Target type   max_iter = 100L,   tol = 1e-6,   M = 80L,   verbose = FALSE ) # Method 1: Moment-based target using chi-square discretization fit_kl <- DPprior_a2_kl(J = 50, target = list(mu_K = 5, var_K = 8),                           method = "chisq") cat("A2-KL solution: Gamma(", round(fit_kl$parameters$a, 4), ", ",     round(fit_kl$parameters$b, 4), ")\n", sep = "") #> A2-KL solution: Gamma(2.2363, 1.7627) cat("Final KL divergence:",     format(fit_kl$residuals$distribution$kl, scientific = TRUE), "\n") #> Final KL divergence: 5.029658e-03  # Method 2: Direct PMF target target_pmf <- discretize_chisq(J = 50, df = 6.25, scale = 0.8) fit_kl2 <- DPprior_a2_kl(J = 50, target = target_pmf, method = "pmf")

title: The Applied Researcher's Guide to Cluster-Count Elicitation
text: Eliciting Gamma(,b)(, b) hyperprior α\alpha requires specifying two pieces information: location (expect number clusters ) scale (certain expectation). DPprior package operationalizes two quantities: Expected number clusters (μK\mu_K): best guess number distinct groups Uncertainty expectation (σK2\sigma^2_K confidence level): sure guess need ? Gamma distribution two parameters, single piece information insufficient uniquely determine prior. Think way: saying “expect 15 clusters” correspond many different priors—tightly concentrated prior strongly believes exactly 15 clusters, diffuse prior merely centers around 15 allows substantial deviation. mean (μ_K = 15) different levels uncertainty leads different priors α.
code: # Compare priors with same mean but different variances J <- 100 mu_K <- 15  targets <- list(   "High Uncertainty (var_K = 70)" =     DPprior_target_K(J, mu_K = mu_K, var_K = 70),   "Medium Uncertainty (var_K = 35)" =     DPprior_target_K(J, mu_K = mu_K, var_K = 35),   "Low Uncertainty (var_K = 21)" =     DPprior_target_K(J, mu_K = mu_K, var_K = 21) ) fits <- lapply(targets, function(target_K) {   DPprior_fit(J, target_K = target_K, check_diagnostics = FALSE) })  # Pre-compute log Stirling numbers for PMF calculation logS <- compute_log_stirling(J)  # Create data for alpha prior plot alpha_grid <- seq(0.01, 20, length.out = 300) alpha_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(nm) {   fit <- fits[[nm]]   data.frame(     alpha = alpha_grid,     density = dgamma(alpha_grid, shape = fit$parameters$a,                      rate = fit$parameters$b),     Uncertainty = nm   ) })) alpha_df$Uncertainty <- factor(alpha_df$Uncertainty, levels = names(fits))  # Create data for K PMF plot k_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(nm) {   fit <- fits[[nm]]   pmf <- pmf_K_marginal(     J, fit$parameters$a, fit$parameters$b, logS = logS   )   data.frame(     K = 1:length(pmf),     probability = pmf,     Uncertainty = nm   ) })) k_df$Uncertainty <- factor(k_df$Uncertainty, levels = names(fits))  # Plot alpha priors p1 <- ggplot(alpha_df, aes(x = alpha, y = density, color = Uncertainty)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   scale_color_manual(values = palette_3) +   labs(x = expression(alpha), y = "Density",        title = expression("Prior Density for " * alpha)) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom",         legend.title = element_blank(),         legend.direction = "vertical")  # Plot K PMF p2 <- ggplot(k_df[k_df$K <= 35, ], aes(x = K, y = probability, color = Uncertainty)) +   geom_point(size = 1.5) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +   scale_color_manual(values = palette_3) +   labs(x = "Number of Clusters (K)", y = "Probability",        title = "Implied PMF of K") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom",         legend.title = element_blank(),         legend.direction = "vertical")  # Arrange plots side by side gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)

what: 7.2 Complete Example: From Problem to Solution
title: Diagnosing Your Prior: Avoiding Unintended Consequences
text: Let us walk complete example diagnostic-driven refinement. Step 1: Initial K-prior Step 2: Run diagnostics Step 3: Identify problem K-prior larger--intended W_SB tail probability. Step 4: Apply dual-anchor refinement Step 5: Read verified hard-fit evidence Step 6: Visualize improvement Comparison weight distributions dual-anchor refinement.
code:
# Researcher expects ~5 clusters with moderate uncertainty target_K <- DPprior_target_K(J = 50, mu_K = 5, var_K = 8) fit1 <- DPprior_fit(   J = 50, target_K = target_K, method = "A2-MN",   check_diagnostics = FALSE )  cat("Step 1: Initial K-only prior
") #> Step 1: Initial K-only prior cat("Gamma(a =", round(fit1$parameters$a, 4), ", b =",     round(fit1$parameters$b, 4), ")

") #> Gamma(a = 2.0361 , b = 1.6051 ) diag1 <- DPprior_diagnostics(fit1) K1 <- diag1$diagnostics$K wsb1 <- diag1$diagnostics$weights wsb1_tail <- prob_wsb_exceeds(   0.5, fit1$parameters$a, fit1$parameters$b )  cat("Step 2: Diagnostics reveal...
") #> Step 2: Diagnostics reveal... cat("  K behavior: E[K] =", round(K1$mean, 2),     ", Var(K) =", round(K1$variance, 2), "✓
") #>   K behavior: E[K] = 5 , Var(K) = 8 ✓ cat("  Weight behavior: P(W_SB > 0.5) =",     round(wsb1_tail, 3), "
") #>   Weight behavior: P(W_SB > 0.5) = 0.481 print(diag1[c("status", "usable", "verified", "message")]) #> $status #> [1] "converged" #>  #> $usable #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $verified #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $message #> [1] "All canonical diagnostic components passed independent selected-versus-verifier checks." plot_w1_prior(fit1) #> Step 3: Problem identification #>   The researcher wanted: ~5 clusters with balanced weights #>   The prior implies: ~5 clusters but a large W_SB tail probability #>   P(W_SB > 0.5) = 48 % is higher than expected for 'balanced' clusters cat("Step 4: Dual-anchor refinement
") #> Step 4: Dual-anchor refinement cat("  Adding constraint: P(W_SB > 0.5) ≤ 0.25

text: concentration parameter α\alpha influences model’s behavior three interconnected ways: Number clusters (KJK_J): Larger α\alpha leads clusters average; smaller α\alpha concentrates mass fewer clusters. Specifically, 𝔼[KJ|α]≈αlog⁡J\mathbb{E}[K_J | \alpha] \approx \alpha \log J large JJ (Antoniak, 1974). Stick-breaking weights: Sethuraman’s (1994) representation, GG constructed via stick-breaking weights (w1,w2,…)(w_1, w_2, \ldots) wh=vh∏ℓ<h(1−vℓ)w_h = v_h \prod_{\ell < h}(1 - v_\ell) vh∼Beta(1,α)v_h \sim \text{Beta}(1, \alpha). Smaller α\alpha produces weights concentrated early atoms (one two clusters dominate); larger α\alpha spreads weights evenly across many clusters. Vicentini & Jermyn (2025) emphasize, weights represent asymptotic relative cluster sizes fundamental quantity distinct cluster count. Posterior shrinkage: prior α\alpha affects much posterior borrows strength across observations. multisite trials, determines degree shrinkage toward common mean—key consideration sites varying sample sizes precision (Lee et al., 2025). figure illustrates different values α\alpha lead dramatically different partition structures. code: # Simulate stick-breaking for different alpha values n_atoms <- 15 alpha_values <- c(0.5, 2, 10)  set.seed(123) sb_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(alpha_values, function(a) {   # Simulate stick-breaking   v <- rbeta(n_atoms, 1, a)   w <- numeric(n_atoms)   w[1] <- v[1]   for (h in 2:n_atoms) {     w[h] <- v[h] * prod(1 - v[1:(h-1)])   }   data.frame(     atom = 1:n_atoms,     weight = w,     alpha = paste0("α = ", a)   ) }))  sb_data$alpha <- factor(sb_data$alpha,                          levels = paste0("α = ", alpha_values))  ggplot(sb_data, aes(x = atom, y = weight, fill = alpha)) +   geom_bar(stat = "identity") +   facet_wrap(~alpha, nrow = 1) +   scale_fill_manual(values = palette_main[1:3]) +   labs(x = "Atom Index",         y = "Stick-Breaking Weight",        title = "Effect of α on Cluster Weight Distribution",        subtitle = "One realization from GEM(α) for each value") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "none",         strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))

code: # Conceptual illustration of prior influence # Create a schematic showing prior vs posterior at different I levels I_levels <- c("Low (I = 0.2)", "Medium (I = 0.5)", "High (I = 0.8)") alpha_grid <- seq(0.01, 6, length.out = 200)  # Create synthetic data for illustration concept_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(I_levels), function(i) {   I <- c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)[i]   prior_weight <- 1 - I      # Prior: Gamma(1.5, 0.8)   prior <- dgamma(alpha_grid, 1.5, 0.8)      # "Likelihood peak" centered at alpha = 2.5   likelihood_center <- 2.5   likelihood_width <- 0.5 + 2 * (1 - I)  # Wider at low I   likelihood <- dnorm(alpha_grid, likelihood_center, likelihood_width)      # Posterior is mixture weighted by informativeness   posterior <- prior_weight * prior + (1 - prior_weight) *                 (likelihood / max(likelihood)) * max(prior)   posterior <- posterior / (sum(posterior) * diff(alpha_grid)[1])      rbind(     data.frame(alpha = alpha_grid, density = prior,                 Type = "Prior", Setting = I_levels[i]),     data.frame(alpha = alpha_grid, density = posterior,                 Type = "Posterior", Setting = I_levels[i])   ) }))  concept_data$Setting <- factor(concept_data$Setting, levels = I_levels) concept_data$Type <- factor(concept_data$Type, levels = c("Prior", "Posterior"))  ggplot(concept_data, aes(x = alpha, y = density, color = Type, linetype = Type)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   facet_wrap(~Setting, nrow = 1) +   scale_color_manual(values = c("Prior" = "#E41A1C", "Posterior" = "#377EB8")) +   scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Prior" = "dashed", "Posterior" = "solid")) +   labs(x = expression(alpha),        y = "Density",        title = "Prior Influence Varies with Informativeness",        subtitle = "In low-I settings, the posterior closely tracks the prior") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom",         legend.title = element_blank(),         strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

title: DPprior: Why Prior Elicitation Matters
text: DPprior package converts intuitive specifications Gamma hyperparameters α∼Gamma(,b)\alpha \sim \text{Gamma}(, b) two-step process: A1 (Closed-form approximation): Using asymptotic relationship KJ∣α≈Poisson(αlog⁡J)K_J \mid \alpha \approx \text{Poisson}(\alpha \log J), Gamma prior α\alpha yields Negative Binomial marginal KJK_J (Vicentini & Jermyn, 2025; Zito et al., 2024), derive initial closed-form estimates (a0,b0)(a_0, b_0). A2 (Newton refinement): Using exact moments computed via Antoniak distribution, refine (,b)(, b) precisely match target (μK,σK2)(\mu_K, \sigma_K^2). approach—call Design-Conditional Elicitation (DCE)—extends original DORO method (Dorazio, 2009; Lee et al., 2025) replacing computationally expensive grid search fast closed-form initialization Newton refinement accurate moment matching. optional dual-anchor extension incorporates weight constraints, addressing “unintended prior” problem identified Vicentini & Jermyn (2025). low-confidence specification deliberately diffuse. therefore use 160 quadrature nodes fit; DPprior independently verifies diagnostics required higher order rather accepting approximate diagnostic bundle. code: # First, fit K-only prior fit_K <- DPprior_fit(J = 50, mu_K = 5, var_K = 8)  # Check the named first-size-biased-weight estimand p_wsb <- prob_wsb_exceeds(   0.5, fit_K$parameters$a, fit_K$parameters$b ) cat("K-only prior: P(W_SB > 0.5) =", round(p_wsb, 3), "\n") #> K-only prior: P(W_SB > 0.5) = 0.481  # A hard scientific requirement is an independently verified inequality. fit_hard <- DPprior_dual_hard(   fit_K,   constraint = list(     metric = "wsb_tail", threshold = 0.5,     relation = "<=", bound = 0.45   ),   M = 20L,   M_verify = 60L,   control = list(     scan_points = 7L, scan_keep = 5L,     profile_starts = 2L, maxit = 40L   ) ) fit_hard[c("status", "usable", "verified")] #> $status #> [1] "boundary" #>  #> $usable #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $verified #> [1] TRUE fit_hard$constraint[c("satisfied", "residual")] #> $satisfied #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $residual #> [1] 2.220446e-15  # A soft question instead declares a fixed-scale trade-off. fit_soft <- DPprior_dual_soft(   fit_K,   target = list(     metric = "wsb_tail", threshold = 0.5,     relation = "target", value = 0.30   ),   lambda = 0.5,   M_fit = 20L,   M_verify = 60L,   max_iter = 40L ) fit_soft[c("status", "usable", "verified")] #> $status #> [1] "converged" #>  #> $usable #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $verified #> [1] TRUE

title: Mathematical Foundations: The K Distribution and Gamma Hyperpriors
text: Poisson-binomial representation conceptually elegant, direct computation Pr⁡(KJ=k|α)\Pr(K_J = k | \alpha) efficiently accomplished via unsigned Stirling numbers first kind. Definition (Unsigned Stirling Numbers). unsigned Stirling number first kind, denoted |s(J,k)||s(J, k)|, counts number permutations JJ elements exactly kk disjoint cycles. satisfy recursion: |s(J,k)|=|s(J−1,k−1)|+(J−1)⋅|s(J−1,k)|, |s(J, k)| = |s(J-1, k-1)| + (J-1) \cdot |s(J-1, k)|,  boundary conditions |s(0,0)|=1|s(0, 0)| = 1, |s(J,0)|=0|s(J, 0)| = 0 J≥1J \geq 1, |s(J,J)|=1|s(J, J)| = 1. Theorem 2 (Antoniak Distribution). k=1,…,Jk = 1, \ldots, J, Pr⁡(KJ=k|α)=|s(J,k)|⋅αk⋅Γ(α)Γ(α+J)=|s(J,k)|⋅αk(α)J, \Pr(K_J = k | \alpha) = |s(J, k)| \cdot \alpha^k \cdot \frac{\Gamma(\alpha)}{\Gamma(\alpha + J)} = |s(J, k)| \cdot \frac{\alpha^k}{(\alpha)_J}, (α)J=α(α+1)⋯(α+J−1)(\alpha)_J = \alpha(\alpha+1)\cdots(\alpha+J-1) rising factorial (Pochhammer symbol). Attribution. classical Antoniak distribution DP partitions (Antoniak, 1974). used extensively DP prior-elicitation work, including Dorazio (2009), Murugiah & Sweeting (2012), Vicentini & Jermyn (2025). general Gibbs-type form Pr⁡(KJ=k)=VJ,k|s(J,k)|\Pr(K_J = k) = V_{J,k} |s(J,k)| discussed Zito, Rigon, & Dunson (2024). Proof sketch. Let pJ,k(α):=Pr⁡(KJ=k|α)p_{J,k}(\alpha) := \Pr(K_J = k | \alpha). CRP transition probabilities, recursion: pJ,k(α)=pJ−1,k−1(α)⋅αα+J−1+pJ−1,k(α)⋅J−1α+J−1. p_{J,k}(\alpha) = p_{J-1,k-1}(\alpha) \cdot \frac{\alpha}{\alpha + J - 1} + p_{J-1,k}(\alpha) \cdot \frac{J-1}{\alpha + J - 1}.  One verifies p̃J,k(α):=|s(J,k)|αkΓ(α)/Γ(α+J)\tilde{p}_{J,k}(\alpha) := |s(J,k)| \alpha^k \Gamma(\alpha)/\Gamma(\alpha+J) satisfies recursion matching initial conditions. ▫\square

Let μJ(α):=𝔼[KJ|α]\mu_J(\alpha) := \mathbb{E}[K_J | \alpha]vJ(α):=Var(KJ|α)v_J(\alpha) := \text{Var}(K_J | \alpha). : μJ(α)=∑=1Jαα+−1, \mu_J(\alpha) = \sum_{=1}^{J} \frac{\alpha}{\alpha + - 1}, vJ(α)=∑=1Jα(−1)(α+−1)2=∑=1Jαα+−1(1−αα+−1). v_J(\alpha) = \sum_{=1}^{J} \frac{\alpha(-1)}{(\alpha + - 1)^2} = \sum_{=1}^{J} \frac{\alpha}{\alpha + - 1}\left(1 - \frac{\alpha}{\alpha + - 1}\right). text: Proposition 2 (Digamma Closed Forms). Let ψ(⋅)\psi(\cdot) denote digamma function ψ1(⋅)\psi_1(\cdot) trigamma function. : μJ(α)=α⋅(ψ(α+J)−ψ(α)), \mu_J(\alpha) = \alpha \cdot \big(\psi(\alpha + J) - \psi(\alpha)\big), vJ(α)=μJ(α)−α2⋅(ψ1(α)−ψ1(α+J)). v_J(\alpha) = \mu_J(\alpha) - \alpha^2 \cdot \big(\psi_1(\alpha) - \psi_1(\alpha + J)\big). Proof. Use identities: ∑r=0J−11α+r=ψ(α+J)−ψ(α),∑r=0J−11(α+r)2=ψ1(α)−ψ1(α+J). \sum_{r=0}^{J-1} \frac{1}{\alpha + r} = \psi(\alpha + J) - \psi(\alpha), \quad \sum_{r=0}^{J-1} \frac{1}{(\alpha + r)^2} = \psi_1(\alpha) - \psi_1(\alpha + J).  variance formula follows rewriting pi(1−pi)=α/(α+−1)−α2/(α+−1)2p_i(1-p_i) = \alpha/(\alpha + - 1) - \alpha^2/(\alpha + - 1)^2. ▫\square Conditional mean variance K_J functions α various sample sizes J.

text: DPprior package provides two solution strategies: A1 (Closed-Form Approximation): Uses Poisson proxy KJ|αK_J | \alpha, Gamma mixing yields Negative Binomial marginal. NegBin moment equations can inverted analytically. provides fast, closed-form solution serves excellent initializer may approximation error small JJ. text: Novel Contribution. A1 closed-form mapping key contribution work. shifted Poisson proxy: KJ−1|α≈Poisson(αcJ), K_J - 1 | \alpha \approx \text{Poisson}(\alpha c_J),  cJ=log⁡Jc_J = \log J (default scaling), α∼Gamma(,b)\alpha \sim \text{Gamma}(, b), marginal becomes: KJ−1≈NegBin(,p),p=bb+cJ. K_J - 1 \approx \text{NegBin}(, p), \quad p = \frac{b}{b + c_J}. Theorem (A1 Closed-Form Inverse). Let μ0=μK−1\mu_0 = \mu_K - 1 (shifted mean). μ0>0\mu_0 > 0 σK2>μ0\sigma^2_K > \mu_0, : =μ02σK2−μ0,b=μ0⋅cJσK2−μ0. = \frac{\mu_0^2}{\sigma^2_K - \mu_0}, \quad b = \frac{\mu_0 \cdot c_J}{\sigma^2_K - \mu_0}. Proof. NegBin proxy, 𝔼[KJ]=1+acJb=1+μ0\mathbb{E}[K_J] = 1 + \frac{ac_J}{b} = 1 + \mu_0 Var(KJ)=μ0+μ02a\text{Var}(K_J) = \mu_0 + \frac{\mu_0^2}{}. Solving aa bb yields result. ▫\square Comparison A1 A2 solutions (J = 50, target μ_K = 8, σ²_K = 15)
code: # Demonstrate A1 closed-form mapping J <- 50 mu_K <- 8 var_K <- 15  # Build one bounded-discrete target and hold it fixed across methods target_K <- DPprior_target_K(J = J, mu_K = mu_K, var_K = var_K)  # A1 and A2 solutions for the same canonical target fit_a1 <- DPprior_fit(   J = J, target_K = target_K, method = "A1",   check_diagnostics = FALSE ) fit_a2 <- DPprior_fit(   J = J, target_K = target_K, method = "A2-MN",   check_diagnostics = FALSE )  comparison <- data.frame(   Method = c("A1 (Closed-Form)", "A2 (Newton)"),   a = c(fit_a1$parameters$a, fit_a2$parameters$a),   b = c(fit_a1$parameters$b, fit_a2$parameters$b),   Achieved_Mean = c(fit_a1$achieved$K$mean, fit_a2$achieved$K$mean),   Achieved_Var = c(fit_a1$achieved$K$variance,                    fit_a2$achieved$K$variance),   Status = c(fit_a1$status, fit_a2$status),   Usable = c(fit_a1$usable, fit_a2$usable),   Verified = c(fit_a1$verified, fit_a2$verified) )  knitr::kable(   comparison,   col.names = c(     "Method", "a", "b", "Achieved E[K]", "Achieved Var(K)",     "Status", "Usable", "Verified"   ),   digits = 4,   caption = sprintf("Comparison of A1 and A2 solutions (J = %d, target μ_K = %d, σ²_K = %d)",                      J, mu_K, var_K) )

text: Novel Contribution. A2 method applies multivariate Newton-Raphson iteration solve: 𝐟(,b):=(M1(,b)−μKV(,b)−σK2)=𝟎. \mathbf{f}(, b) := \begin{pmatrix} M_1(, b) - \mu_K \\ V(, b) - \sigma^2_K \end{pmatrix} = \mathbf{0}. Jacobian 𝐉(,b)=∂𝐟/∂(,b)\mathbf{J}(, b) = \partial \mathbf{f} / \partial (, b) computed via score function method: ∂M1∂=𝔼α[μJ(α)⋅sa(α)],∂M1∂b=𝔼α[μJ(α)⋅sb(α)], \frac{\partial M_1}{\partial } = \mathbb{E}_\alpha[\mu_J(\alpha) \cdot s_a(\alpha)], \quad \frac{\partial M_1}{\partial b} = \mathbb{E}_\alpha[\mu_J(\alpha) \cdot s_b(\alpha)],  sa(α)=log⁡α−ψ()+log⁡bs_a(\alpha) = \log \alpha - \psi() + \log b sb(α)=/b−αs_b(\alpha) = /b - \alpha score functions Gamma distribution. Newton update : (ab)(t+1)=(ab)(t)−𝐉−1𝐟. \begin{pmatrix} \\ b \end{pmatrix}^{(t+1)} = \begin{pmatrix} \\ b \end{pmatrix}^{(t)} - \mathbf{J}^{-1} \mathbf{f}. Initialized A1 solution, convergence typically occurs within 3-5 iterations. Newton iteration convergence A2 method.
code: # Demonstrate Newton convergence (using internal debugging if available) J <- 50 mu_K <- 8 var_K <- 15  # Manual iteration tracking a_init <- fit_a1$parameters$a b_init <- fit_a1$parameters$b  # Compute residuals at each iteration n_iter <- 6 trajectory <- data.frame(   iteration = 0:n_iter,   a = numeric(n_iter + 1),   b = numeric(n_iter + 1),   residual_mean = numeric(n_iter + 1),   residual_var = numeric(n_iter + 1) )  # Use the package's internal Newton solver with tracking # (This is a simplified demonstration) trajectory$a[1] <- a_init trajectory$b[1] <- b_init moments_0 <- exact_K_moments(J, a_init, b_init) trajectory$residual_mean[1] <- moments_0$mean - mu_K trajectory$residual_var[1] <- moments_0$var - var_K  # For display, just show convergence to final values for (i in 2:(n_iter + 1)) {   # Exponential convergence simulation (simplified)   t <- i - 1   trajectory$a[i] <- fit_a2$parameters$a +     (a_init - fit_a2$parameters$a) * (0.1)^t   trajectory$b[i] <- fit_a2$parameters$b +     (b_init - fit_a2$parameters$b) * (0.1)^t   moments_t <- exact_K_moments(J, trajectory$a[i], trajectory$b[i])   trajectory$residual_mean[i] <- moments_t$mean - mu_K   trajectory$residual_var[i] <- moments_t$var - var_K }  trajectory$total_residual <- sqrt(trajectory$residual_mean^2 + trajectory$residual_var^2)  ggplot(trajectory, aes(x = iteration, y = log10(total_residual + 1e-16))) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1, color = "#377EB8") +   geom_point(size = 3, color = "#377EB8") +   labs(x = "Newton Iteration", y = expression(log[10] * "(Residual Norm)"),        title = "A2 Newton Method Convergence",        subtitle = "Quadratic convergence from A1 initialization") +   theme_minimal()

code: # Compute A1 approximation error J_values <- c(25, 50, 100, 200, 300) mu_K <- 8 var_K <- 15  error_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(J_values, function(J) {   target_K <- DPprior_target_K(J = J, mu_K = mu_K, var_K = var_K)   fit_a1 <- DPprior_fit(     J = J, target_K = target_K, method = "A1",     check_diagnostics = FALSE   )   fit_a2 <- DPprior_fit(     J = J, target_K = target_K, method = "A2-MN",     check_diagnostics = FALSE   )      data.frame(     J = J,     Mean_Error_Pct = 100 * abs(fit_a1$achieved$K$mean - mu_K) / mu_K,     Var_Error_Pct = 100 * abs(fit_a1$achieved$K$variance - var_K) / var_K,     a_Relative_Error = abs(fit_a1$parameters$a - fit_a2$parameters$a) /       fit_a2$parameters$a,     b_Relative_Error = abs(fit_a1$parameters$b - fit_a2$parameters$b) /       fit_a2$parameters$b   ) }))  knitr::kable(   error_data,   col.names = c("J", "Mean Error (%)", "Var Error (%)",                  "|a_A1 - a_A2|/a_A2", "|b_A1 - b_A2|/b_A2"),   digits = c(0, 2, 2, 4, 4),   caption = sprintf("A1 approximation error (target μ_K = %d, σ²_K = %d)", mu_K, var_K) )

code: # Monte Carlo simulation using Poisson-Binomial representation n_sim <- 100000 J <- 50 alpha <- 2  # Bernoulli success probabilities p <- alpha / (alpha + (1:J) - 1)  # Simulate K_J set.seed(123) K_samples <- replicate(n_sim, sum(runif(J) < p))  # Compare distributions k_range <- 1:20 pmf_stirling <- pmf_K_given_alpha(J, alpha, logS)[k_range + 1] pmf_mc <- tabulate(K_samples, nbins = max(K_samples))[k_range] / n_sim  comparison_df <- data.frame(   k = rep(k_range, 2),   pmf = c(pmf_stirling, pmf_mc),   Method = rep(c("Stirling (exact)", "Monte Carlo (n=100K)"), each = length(k_range)) )  ggplot(comparison_df, aes(x = k, y = pmf, color = Method, shape = Method)) +   geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +   scale_color_manual(values = c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8")) +   scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +   labs(     x = expression(k),     y = "Probability",     title = expression("Verification: Stirling vs. Poisson-Binomial Monte Carlo"),     subtitle = sprintf("J = %d, α = %g", J, alpha)   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     legend.position = "bottom",     plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),     plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)   ) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_point()`). # Numerical comparison max_diff <- max(abs(pmf_stirling - pmf_mc)) cat(sprintf("\nMaximum absolute difference between methods: %.2e\n", max_diff)) #>  #> Maximum absolute difference between methods: NA

title: Weight Distributions: w₁, ρ, and the Dual-Anchor Framework
text: Sethuraman’s (1994) stick-breaking representation DP, random probability measure G∼DP(α,G0)G \sim \text{DP}(\alpha, G_0) can written : G=∑h=1∞whδθh, G = \sum_{h=1}^{\infty} w_h \, \delta_{\theta_h},  {θh}h=1∞∼iidG0\{\theta_h\}_{h=1}^{\infty} \stackrel{iid}{\sim} G_0 atom locations {wh}h=1∞\{w_h\}_{h=1}^{\infty} stick-breaking weights constructed : vh∼iidBeta(1,α),w1=v1,wh=vh∏ℓ<h(1−vℓ)(h≥2). v_h \stackrel{iid}{\sim} \text{Beta}(1, \alpha), \quad  w_1 = v_1, \quad  w_h = v_h \prod_{\ell < h}(1 - v_\ell) \quad (h \geq 2). sequence (w1,w2,…)(w_1, w_2, \ldots) follows GEM(α\alpha) distribution (Griffiths-Engen-McCloskey), represents size-biased random permutation Poisson-Dirichlet distribution (Pitman, 1996).

code: # Demonstrate the stick-breaking construction n_atoms <- 15 alpha_values <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)  set.seed(123) sb_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(alpha_values, function(a) {   v <- rbeta(n_atoms, 1, a)   w <- numeric(n_atoms)   w[1] <- v[1]   for (h in 2:n_atoms) {     w[h] <- v[h] * prod(1 - v[1:(h-1)])   }   data.frame(     atom = 1:n_atoms,     weight = w,     alpha = paste0("α = ", a)   ) }))  sb_data$alpha <- factor(sb_data$alpha, levels = paste0("α = ", alpha_values))  ggplot(sb_data, aes(x = factor(atom), y = weight, fill = alpha)) +   geom_bar(stat = "identity") +   facet_wrap(~alpha, nrow = 1) +   scale_fill_manual(values = palette_main) +   labs(     x = "Atom Index (h)",      y = expression(w[h]),     title = "Stick-Breaking Weights in GEM Order",     subtitle = "Single realization per α; NOT ranked by size"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "none")

Let α∼Gamma(,b)\alpha \sim \text{Gamma}(, b). : Density: p(w1∣,b)=aba(1−w1)[b−log⁡(1−w1)]+1,w1∈(0,1). p(w_1 \mid , b) = \frac{\, b^}{(1 - w_1)[b - \log(1-w_1)]^{+1}}, \quad w_1 \(0, 1). CDF: Fw1(x∣,b)=P(w1≤x∣,b)=1−(bb−log⁡(1−x)). F_{w_1}(x \mid , b) = P(w_1 \leq x \mid , b) = 1 - \left(\frac{b}{b - \log(1-x)}\right)^. First-size-biased-weight survival function: P(w1>t∣,b)=(bb−log⁡(1−t)). P(w_1 > t \mid , b) = \left(\frac{b}{b - \log(1-t)}\right)^. Quantile function: Qw1(u∣,b)=1−exp⁡(b[1−(1−u)−1/]). title: Weight Distributions: w₁, ρ, and the Dual-Anchor Framework
text: co-clustering probability provides alternative, often intuitive, anchor weight-based elicitation. Definition 1 (Co-clustering probability / Simpson index). ρ:=∑h=1∞wh2∈(0,1). \rho := \sum_{h=1}^{\infty} w_h^2 \(0, 1). Interpretation. Conditional random measure GG, Z1,Z2Z_1, Z_2 ..d. cluster labels P(Z=k∣G)=wkP(Z = k \mid G) = w_k, : P(Z1=Z2∣G)=∑k≥1wk2=ρ. P(Z_1 = Z_2 \mid G) = \sum_{k \geq 1} w_k^2 = \rho. Thus ρ\rho probability two randomly chosen units belong latent cluster. quantity translates directly applied elicitation: “seeing data, probability two randomly selected sites study belong effect group?”

title: Weight Distributions: w₁, ρ, and the Dual-Anchor Framework
text: Proposition 2 (Conditional expectation ρ\rho; Kingman, 1975; Pitman, 1996). 𝔼[ρ∣α]=11+α. \mathbb{E}[\rho \mid \alpha] = \frac{1}{1 + \alpha}. Proof. Using stick-breaking construction: 𝔼[wk2∣α]=𝔼[vk2]⋅∏ℓ<k𝔼[(1−vℓ)2]. \mathbb{E}[w_k^2 \mid \alpha] = \mathbb{E}[v_k^2] \cdot \prod_{\ell < k} \mathbb{E}[(1-v_\ell)^2]. v∼Beta(1,α)v \sim \text{Beta}(1, \alpha): 𝔼[v2]=2(1+α)(2+α),𝔼[(1−v)2]=α2+α. \mathbb{E}[v^2] = \frac{2}{(1+\alpha)(2+\alpha)}, \quad  \mathbb{E}[(1-v)^2] = \frac{\alpha}{2+\alpha}. Summing geometric series: 𝔼[ρ∣α]=∑k=1∞2(1+α)(2+α)(α2+α)k−1=11+α. \mathbb{E}[\rho \mid \alpha] = \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{2}{(1+\alpha)(2+\alpha)}  \left(\frac{\alpha}{2+\alpha}\right)^{k-1} = \frac{1}{1+\alpha}. ▫\square Corollary 1 (Key identity). conditional expectations w1w_1 ρ\rho equal: 𝔼[w1∣α]=𝔼[ρ∣α]=11+α. \mathbb{E}[w_1 \mid \alpha] = \mathbb{E}[\rho \mid \alpha] = \frac{1}{1+\alpha}. identity coincidental—quantities measure “concentration” random measure GG. Proposition 3 (Conditional variance ρ\rho). 𝔼[ρ2∣α]=α+6(α+1)(α+2)(α+3), \mathbb{E}[\rho^2 \mid \alpha] = \frac{\alpha + 6}{(\alpha+1)(\alpha+2)(\alpha+3)}, Var(ρ∣α)=2α(α+1)2(α+2)(α+3). \text{Var}(\rho \mid \alpha) = \frac{2\alpha}{(\alpha+1)^2(\alpha+2)(\alpha+3)}. Proof. Using distributional recursion ρ=dv2+(1−v)2ρ′\rho \stackrel{d}{=} v^2 + (1-v)^2 \rho' v∼Beta(1,α)v \sim \text{Beta}(1, \alpha) ρ′\rho' independent copy ρ\rho. Squaring taking expectations yields result. See Appendix associated research notes full derivation. ▫\square Conditional mean variance ρ functions α.

title: Weight Distributions: w₁, ρ, and the Dual-Anchor Framework
text: Computing unconditional moments w1w_1 ρ\rho Gamma hyperprior requires evaluating expectations form 𝔼[1/(α+c)]\mathbb{E}[1/(\alpha + c)]. Definition 2 (IcI_c functional). Ic(,b):=𝔼[1α+c],α∼Gamma(,b) c>0. I_c(, b) := \mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{\alpha + c}\right], \quad  \text{} \alpha \sim \text{Gamma}(, b) \text{ } c > 0. Lemma 1 (Closed-form expression IcI_c; work). Ic(,b)=baca−1ebcΓ(1−,bc), I_c(, b) = b^\, c^{-1} \, e^{bc} \, \Gamma(1-, bc),  Γ(s,x)=∫x∞ts−1e−tdt\Gamma(s, x) = \int_x^\infty t^{s-1} e^{-t} \, dt upper incomplete gamma function. Proof. : Ic(,b)=baΓ()∫0∞αa−1e−bαα+cdα. I_c(, b) = \frac{b^}{\Gamma()} \int_0^\infty \frac{\alpha^{-1} e^{-b\alpha}}{\alpha + c} \, d\alpha. what: 4.3 Second Moments and Variance of ρ\rho
title: Weight Distributions: w₁, ρ, and the Dual-Anchor Framework
text: Proposition 4 (Unconditional second moment ρ\rho; work). Using partial fraction decomposition: α+6(α+1)(α+2)(α+3)=52(α+1)−4α+2+32(α+3), \frac{\alpha + 6}{(\alpha+1)(\alpha+2)(\alpha+3)} = \frac{5}{2(\alpha+1)} - \frac{4}{\alpha+2} + \frac{3}{2(\alpha+3)}, obtain: 𝔼[ρ2∣,b]=52I1(,b)−4I2(,b)+32I3(,b). \mathbb{E}[\rho^2 \mid , b] = \frac{5}{2} I_1(, b) - 4 I_2(, b) + \frac{3}{2} I_3(, b). Hence unconditional variance: Var(ρ∣,b)=𝔼[ρ2∣,b]−{𝔼[ρ∣,b]}2. \text{Var}(\rho \mid , b) = \mathbb{E}[\rho^2 \mid , b] - \{\mathbb{E}[\rho \mid , b]\}^2. Key design implication. distribution ρ∣,b\rho \mid , b closed-form, mean variance closed-form (“moment-closed”). sufficient moment-based calibration diagnostics.

title: A1 Closed-Form Prior Elicitation — DPprior_a1
text: A1 method uses shifted Negative Binomial approximation: $$K_J - 1 \mid \alpha \approx \text{Poisson}(\alpha \cdot c_J)$$ \(\alpha \sim \text{Gamma}(, b)\), marginal becomes: $$K_J - 1 \approx \text{NegBin}(, b/(b + c_J))$$

title: A1 Closed-Form Prior Elicitation — DPprior_a1
text: Let \(m = \mu_K - 1\) (shifted mean) \(D = \sigma^2_K - m\). \(D > 0\) (overdispersion): $$= m^2 / D, \quad b = m \cdot c_J / D$$ \(D \leq 0\), target infeasible A1. default typed error. Projection occurs projection = "nearest" emits exactly one typed projection warning.

title: A1 Closed-Form Prior Elicitation — DPprior_a1
text: NegBin model requires overdispersion: \(\sigma^2_K > \mu_K - 1\). High-confidence specifications (low variance) may violate constraint A1 proxy, even though may feasible exact DP.

title: Build Quadrature for Gamma(a, b) Integration — build_gamma_quadrature
text: Numeric; shape parameter Gamma distribution (must > 0). b Numeric; rate parameter Gamma distribution (must > 0). M Integer; number quadrature nodes (default: 80).

title: Build Quadrature for Gamma(a, b) Integration — build_gamma_quadrature
text: list components: Shape parameter. b Rate parameter. alpha_nodes Numeric vector transformed nodes \(\alpha_m = x_m / b\) \(\alpha\) scale. weights_normalized Numeric vector normalized weights sum 1. list also carries quadrature_metadata attribute selected M, Gamma parameterization, node-cache provenance, normalization method. List component names unchanged.

title: Build Quadrature for Gamma(a, b) Integration — build_gamma_quadrature
text: \(\alpha \sim \text{Gamma}(, b)\): $$E[g(\alpha)] = \frac{1}{\Gamma()} \int_0^\infty g(x/b) x^{-1} e^{-x} dx$$ Using generalized Laguerre quadrature parameter \(\alpha_{\text{param}} = - 1\): $$E[g(\alpha)] \approx \sum_{m=1}^M \tilde{w}_m g(\alpha_m)$$ \(\alpha_m = x_m / b\) \(\tilde{w}_m\) normalized weights summing 1. weights normalized log-space numerical stability. Accuracy M changes integrand-dependent generally monotone.

title: Build Quadrature for Gamma(a, b) Integration — build_gamma_quadrature
code: # Build quadrature for Gamma(2.5, 1.5) quad <- build_gamma_quadrature(2.5, 1.5)  # Check weights sum to 1 sum(quad$weights_normalized) #> [1] 1  # Check mean: E[alpha] should be a/b = 2.5/1.5 sum(quad$weights_normalized * quad$alpha_nodes) #> [1] 1.666667

title: Mean-Linearization Error Bound — compute_linearization_bound
text: Let \(\lambda = \lambda_J(\alpha)\) (exact shifted mean) \(\lambda' = \alpha c_J\) (A1 approximate mean). KL divergence : $$KL(\text{Poisson}(\lambda) || \text{Poisson}(\lambda')) =       \lambda \log(\lambda/\lambda') + \lambda' - \lambda$$ Pinsker's inequality: $$d_{TV}(\text{Poisson}(\lambda), \text{Poisson}(\lambda')) \le \sqrt{KL/2}$$ Numerical safeguards handle edge cases \(\lambda\) \(c_J\) zero.

title: Compute Log Stirling Numbers (First Kind, Unsigned) — compute_log_stirling

text: J_max Maximum J value (non-negative integer, 500).

title: Compute Log Stirling Numbers (First Kind, Unsigned) — compute_log_stirling
text: lower triangular matrix dimension (J_max+1) x (J_max+1). Entry [J+1, k+1] contains \(\log|s(J,k)|\) (using R's 1-based indexing). Invalid entries (k > J k < 1 J >= 1) contain -Inf.

title: Compute Log Stirling Numbers (First Kind, Unsigned) — compute_log_stirling
text: unsigned Stirling numbers first kind \(|s(J,k)|\) count number permutations \(J\) elements exactly \(k\) disjoint cycles. Uses log-space recurrence relation: $$L_{J,k} = \text{logsumexp}(L_{J-1,k-1}, \log(J-1) + L_{J-1,k})$$ \(L_{J,k} = \log|s(J,k)|\). Boundary conditions: \(|s(0,0)| = 1\) \(\rightarrow\) L[1,1] = 0 \(|s(J,0)| = 0\) \(J \geq 1\) \(\rightarrow\) L[J+1,1] = -Inf \(|s(J,J)| = 1\) \(J\) \(\rightarrow\) L[J+1,J+1] = 0 Complexity: O(J_max^2) time space. largest table computed session cached internally reused smaller requests. bounded cache retains one matrix.

title: Compute Log Stirling Numbers (First Kind, Unsigned) — compute_log_stirling
text: Antoniak, C. E. (1974). Mixtures Dirichlet Processes Applications Bayesian Nonparametric Problems. Annals Statistics, 2(6), 1152-1174.

title: Compute Log Stirling Numbers (First Kind, Unsigned) — compute_log_stirling
code: # Compute Stirling numbers up to J=10 logS <- compute_log_stirling(10)  # Access |s(4,2)| = 11 exp(logS[5, 3]) #> [1] 11  # Access |s(5,3)| = 35 exp(logS[6, 4]) #> [1] 35

title: Poissonization Error Bound (Chen-Stein / Le Cam Bound) — compute_poissonization_bound
text: CRP representation, \(S_J = \sum_{=2}^J I_i\) \(I_i \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p_i)\) \(p_i = \alpha / (\alpha + - 1)\). standard Chen-Stein/Le Cam bound gives: $$d_{TV}(S_J, \text{Poisson}(\lambda)) \le       \frac{1 - e^{-\lambda}}{\lambda} \sum_{=2}^J p_i^2$$ \(\lambda = \sum_{=2}^J p_i = E[S_J | \alpha]\). prefactor \((1 - e^{-\lambda})/\lambda\) always (0, 1] approaches 1 \(\lambda \0\). provides tighter bound simply using \(\sum p_i^2\) alone. also larger submitted manuscript Appendix D bound \(\min(1,1/\lambda)\sum p_i^2\) (Equation D10), implementation strengthened Chen–Stein crosswalk rather different estimand. returned value capped 1 (since total variation always 0 1).

title: Poissonization Error Bound (Chen-Stein / Le Cam Bound) — compute_poissonization_bound
text: Le Cam, L. (1960). approximation theorem Poisson binomial distribution. Pacific Journal Mathematics, 10(4), 1181-1197. Chen, L. H. Y. (1975). Poisson approximation dependent trials. Annals Probability, 3(3), 534-545. Lee, J. (2026). Design-Conditional Prior Elicitation Dirichlet Process Mixtures. arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.06301.

title: Gauss-Laguerre Quadrature Nodes and Weights — gauss_laguerre_nodes
text: algorithm constructs tridiagonal Jacobi matrix \(J\) size \(M \times M\): Diagonal: \(a_k = 2k + 1 + \alpha\) \(k = 0, \ldots, M-1\) -diagonal: \(b_k = \sqrt{k(k + \alpha)}\) \(k = 1, \ldots, M-1\) Eigendecomposition \(J = V D V^T\) yields: Nodes = eigenvalues (diagonal \(D\)) Weights = \(\Gamma(\alpha + 1) \cdot V[1,:]^2\) generalized Laguerre polynomials \(L_n^{(\alpha)}(x)\) orthogonal respect weight function \(w(x) = x^\alpha e^{-x}\) \([0, \infty)\).

title: Gauss-Laguerre Quadrature Nodes and Weights — gauss_laguerre_nodes

title: Compute Marginal Moments and Jacobian Simultaneously — moments_with_jacobian
text: named list components: mean Marginal mean \(E[K_J]\) var Marginal variance \(Var(K_J)\) jacobian 2x2 Jacobian matrix structure: $$J_F = \begin{bmatrix} \partial M_1/\partial & \partial M_1/\partial b \\                                  \partial V/\partial & \partial V/\partial b \end{bmatrix}$$ derivative_diagnostics Order-refinement status, tolerances, quadrature orders used score derivatives. conditioning Scale-aware singularity diagnostics shape-rate solver log-parameterizations.

title: Compute Marginal Moments and Jacobian Simultaneously — moments_with_jacobian
text: function uses score identity (Lee, 2026, Section 3.2, Corollary 1) compute derivatives without finite differences: $$\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta} E[f(\alpha)] = E[f(\alpha) \cdot s_\theta(\alpha)]$$ Jacobian components computed : \(\partial M_1/\partial \theta =     E[(\mu_J(\alpha)-1) \cdot s_\theta(\alpha)]\) \(\partial V/\partial \theta = \partial E[v_J]/\partial \theta +              \partial E[\mu_J^2]/\partial \theta - 2 M_1 \partial M_1/\partial \theta\) Subtracting exact zero-concentration limits exact control variate \(E[s_\theta(\alpha)]=0\). removes spurious constant times log(alpha) term otherwise dominates finite-order shape-score quadrature. Derivatives recomputed distinct higher order supported ceiling permits; returned diagnostic converged full scheduled refinement available two orders meet release mixed error budget 5e-5 + 2e-3 * max(abs(selected), abs(verification)) componentwise. Numerical Considerations: score function s_a contains log(alpha), causes slower quadrature convergence compared moment computation. score calculation uses least 80 nodes distinct higher order available; orders retained diagnostics. Conditional moments use stable finite sums without small-alpha threshold negative clipping. returned marginal variance uses non-negative within/decomposition rather cancellation-prone second-moment subtraction. Conditioning status based solver-relevant log-parameter Jacobian, unscaled determinant alone.

text: Lee, J. (2026). Design-Conditional Prior Elicitation Dirichlet Process Mixtures. arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.06301.

title: PMF of K Given Alpha (Antoniak Distribution) — pmf_K_given_alpha
text: Computes \(P(K_J = k \mid \alpha)\) \(k = 0, 1, \ldots, J\) using Antoniak distribution derived Dirichlet process.

title: PMF of K Given Alpha (Antoniak Distribution) — pmf_K_given_alpha
text: J Integer; sample size (number observations, must >= 1). alpha Numeric; DP concentration parameter (must positive scalar). logS Matrix; pre-computed log-Stirling matrix compute_log_stirling. normalize Logical; TRUE (default), apply final probability-scale normalization. FALSE, directly exponentiate already normalized log-PMF.

title: PMF of K Given Alpha (Antoniak Distribution) — pmf_K_given_alpha
text: Numeric vector length \(J+1\) containing \(P(K_J = k \mid \alpha)\) \(k = 0, 1, \ldots, J\). Entry [1] corresponds \(k=0\) always equals 0. mathematical support \(\{1,\ldots,J\}\). vector sums 1 floating-point tolerance either normalization mode.

title: PMF of K Given Alpha (Antoniak Distribution) — pmf_K_given_alpha
text: Antoniak distribution gives exact PMF number occupied clusters \(K_J\) Dirichlet process concentration parameter \(\alpha\): $$P(K_J = k \mid \alpha) = |s(J,k)| \frac{\alpha^k}{(\alpha)_J}$$ \(|s(J,k)|\) unsigned Stirling number first kind \((\alpha)_J\) rising factorial. Key properties: \(P(K_J = 0) = 0\) always (least one cluster exists) \(P(K_J = J) > 0\) \(\alpha > 0\) \(\alpha \0^+\), mass concentrates \(K_J = 1\) \(\alpha \\infty\), mass concentrates \(K_J = J\) Extremely small support probabilities may underflow structural zeros probability scale. Setting normalize = TRUE applies final normalization exponentiation; normalize = FALSE skips final correction return unnormalized Antoniak weights.

title: PMF of K Given Alpha (Antoniak Distribution) — pmf_K_given_alpha
text: Antoniak, C. E. (1974). Mixtures Dirichlet Processes Applications Bayesian Nonparametric Problems. Annals Statistics, 2(6), 1152-1174.

title: PMF of K Given Alpha (Antoniak Distribution) — pmf_K_given_alpha
code: # Compute PMF for J=50, alpha=2 logS <- compute_log_stirling(50) pmf <- pmf_K_given_alpha(50, 2.0, logS)  # Verify normalization sum(pmf)  # Should be 1 #> [1] 1  # Verify P(K=0) = 0 pmf[1]    # Should be 0 #> [1] 0  # Most likely number of clusters (mode) which.max(pmf) - 1  # Subtract 1 for 0-indexing #> [1] 7  # Compare with moments k_vals <- 0:50 mean_K <- sum(k_vals * pmf) var_K <- sum(k_vals^2 * pmf) - mean_K^2  # These should match digamma formulas mean_K_given_alpha(50, 2.0) #> [1] 7.037626 var_K_given_alpha(50, 2.0) #> [1] 4.535558

title: Marginal PMF of K_J under Gamma Hyperprior — pmf_K_marginal
text: Uses Gauss-Laguerre quadrature numerically evaluate: $$P(K_J = k \mid , b) = \int_0^\infty P(K_J = k \mid \alpha) \cdot g_{,b}(\alpha) d\alpha$$ $$\approx \sum_{m=1}^M \tilde{w}_m \cdot P(K_J = k \mid \alpha_m)$$ \(P(K_J = k \mid \alpha)\) Antoniak distribution Module 04 \((\alpha_m, \tilde{w}_m)\) transformed quadrature nodes normalized weights Module 02. Implementation: mixing performed log-space numerical stability. critical large J extreme parameter values. "converged" result additionally requires higher-order PMF L1 agreement PMF-versus-direct-moment agreement quadrature orders. Key properties: \(P(K_J = 0) = 0\) always (least one cluster exists) PMF sums 1 Moments PMF match exact_K_moments() within numerical tolerance Mode typically near \(E[K_J]\) may differ

title: Random Generation from rho Distribution — rrho
text: n Integer; number samples generate. Numeric; shape parameter Gamma prior alpha (> 0). b Numeric; rate parameter Gamma prior alpha (b > 0). n_sticks Integer; minimum number sticks generated draw. sampler continues adaptively remaining squared mass remainder_tol. Default 500. remainder_tol Numeric; maximum allowed deterministic upper bound omitted contribution rho. ungenerated weights sum remainder \(R\), contribution satisfies \(0 <= \sum_{\mathrm{tail}} w_h^2 <= R^2\). Default 1e-10. max_sticks Integer; hard per-draw stick ceiling. Default 100,000. strict Logical; TRUE (default), reaching max_sticks remainder contract met raises typed dpprior_rho_truncation_error. FALSE, finite lower approximation returned status "approximate" deterministic remainder bound "rrho_diagnostics" attribute.

title: Random Generation from rho Distribution — rrho
text: Numeric vector length n. "rrho_diagnostics" attribute records adaptive method, status, tolerance, sticks used, per-draw deterministic omitted-rho bounds ordinary log scales. positive bound smaller floating-point range, ordinary-scale representation rounded upward smallest positive double rather silently reported zero.

title: Random Generation from rho Distribution — rrho
text: Uses hierarchical representation: alpha ~ Gamma(, b) v_h | alpha ~ Beta(1, alpha) independently w_1 = v_1, w_h = v_h * prod(1 - v_l) l < h Generate least n_sticks terms continue unallocated remainder \(R\) obeys \(R^2 <= remainder_tol\) Return partial sum; omitted contribution \([0,R^2]\) Thus finite-stick error controlled draw draw rather silently discarded. Useful Monte Carlo validation analytical formulas.

title: Score Function with Respect to Shape Parameter a — score_a
text: Gamma(shape = , rate = b) distribution density $$g_{,b}(\alpha) = \frac{b^}{\Gamma()} \alpha^{-1} e^{-b\alpha},$$ score function respect : $$s_a(\alpha) = \log b - \psi() + \log \alpha,$$ \(\psi\) digamma function. fundamental property score functions expectation zero: $$E_{\alpha \sim g_{,b}}[s_a(\alpha)] = 0.$$ Numerical Note: log(alpha) term causes slow quadrature convergence raw score expectation, especially small shape. Production derivatives use zero-limit control variate separately recorded order-refinement check rather treating larger order exact.

title: Conditional Variance of K_J Given Alpha — var_K_given_alpha
text: classical trigamma closed form : $$v_J(\alpha) = \mu_J(\alpha) - \alpha^2\{\psi_1(\alpha) - \psi_1(\alpha+J)\}$$ \(\psi_1(\cdot)\) trigamma function. equivalent direct summation: $$v_J(\alpha) = \sum_{=1}^{J} \frac{\alpha(-1)}{(\alpha + - 1)^2}$$ Key property: \(0 \leq v_J(\alpha) < \mu_J(\alpha)\) \(\alpha > 0\). lower inequality strict J > 1; J = 1, \(K_J=1\) deterministically variance zero. Limiting behavior: \(\alpha \0^+\): \(v_J(\alpha) \0\) \(\alpha \\infty\): \(v_J(\alpha) \0\) implementation evaluates Bernoulli variance contribution non-negative ratio term. remains stable small large alpha without clipping cancellation artifacts zero.

title: Convert Variance Inflation Factor to Variance — vif_to_variance
text: mu_K Numeric; target prior mean \(K_J\). vif Numeric; Variance Inflation Factor (must >= 1 A1 feasibility).

title: Convert Variance Inflation Factor to Variance — vif_to_variance
text: Numeric; variance \(K_J\) computed \((\mu_K - 1) \times \text{VIF}\).

title: Convert Variance Inflation Factor to Variance — vif_to_variance
text: VIF defined : $$\text{VIF} = \frac{\sigma^2_K}{\mu_K - 1}$$ Interpretation: VIF = 1 Poisson variance (exact boundary A1) VIF > 1 Overdispersion (required A1 feasibility) VIF < 1 Underdispersion (infeasible A1, allowed)

title: Convert Variance Inflation Factor to Variance — vif_to_variance
code: # VIF = 2 means variance is twice the Poisson variance vif_to_variance(mu_K = 5, vif = 2)  # Returns 8 #> [1] 8  # Use with DPprior_a1 fit <- DPprior_a1(J = 50, mu_K = 5, var_K = vif_to_variance(5, 2))

what: Minor Release: Target PMFs, Feasibility Checks, And Release Hygiene
title: DPprior 1.1.0
text: Added wrapper-level custom target PMF workflow DPprior_fit(). target_pmf can now supplied without mu_K; wrapper dispatches method = "A2-KL" stores normalized PMF target implied moments. Made target_pmf canonical target supplied. Explicit mu_K var_K values now treated consistency checks conflicting values produce clear errors instead silently overwritten. Tightened length J + 1 target PMF validation. Inputs validated structural K = 0 entry dropped, positive mass K = 0 rejected K_J supported {1, ..., J}. Standardized moment feasibility across DPprior_fit(), DPprior_a1(), DPprior_a2_newton(), construct_target_pmf(), DPprior_a2_kl(method = "chisq"). Moment workflows now consistently require 1 < mu_K < J, since mu_K = J implies zero variance outside positive-variance elicitation workflow. Enforced fixed-mean variance bound var_K <= (mu_K - 1) * (J - mu_K) consistently surfaced near-boundary confidence settings clearer feasibility errors. Updated DPprior_fit() non-converged low-variance A2-MN calibrations reported errors rather returned usable wrapper fits. Improved base graphics behavior show = FALSE plotting paths return without opening graphics device leaving default Rplots.pdf artifacts. Fixed source-build boundary installed vignettes. Source tarballs now retain generated inst/doc outputs required R CMD check, local development artifacts remain excluded public release outputs. Updated package metadata, README citation version, release-facing documentation 1.1.0 minor release. Added exact Institute Education Sciences support acknowledgement disclaimer.
